chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abi Baseer, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who slanders another man with adultery, he said: He is whipped, as established in the Book of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
He said, And I asked Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who slanders a young slave girl, so he said: He is not whipped unless she has reached maturity or is near to it.

key_terms.قَذَفَ: To slander or accuse of adultery
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: He is whipped (receives the hadd penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd penalty for slandering a man versus a young girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the application of the hadd al-qadhf (flogging for slander) by distinguishing between adult and pre-pubescent females, establishing that the penalty applies only when the accused girl has reached or is near puberty (bulugh). It reflects the Shia juristic view that the legal capacity to be slandered in this context requires sexual maturity, thereby linking the physical penalty to the biological status of the individual rather than mere age.
